chapter: Opinions on playing and old New Orleans
title: New York's hard-nosed scene; Bunk, the Eagle Band and Bolden's band
summary: Foster says New York drops players, as with Bunk, and discusses the Eagle Band's poor reading and Bolden band members.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: New York is a funny town for music. You either eat or you're out. You know what I mean? You see, because you get in- I mean mother, yeah. See, you get in on that ground floor with those guys around New York. It's anywhere else, because when they put the thumbs down on you. See, just like Bunk, I tell you, Bunk got so bad nobody wouldn't hire him. Yeah. Well, you do that same thing around New York. That ain't just started. That been started a long time ago. You're going to get out of town and go do something. That's how Bunk went off with a circus and was playing around there with a circus for a long time. Well nobody didn't know where Bunk went for a while, they didn't.

And after Bunk left off the Spirit Band, and went with Eagle Band, nobody didn't worry about him, because everybody knows what kind of band that Eagle Band was, it wasn't nothing. They'd play, see, because what's that Nixon, the violin player? Andrew Nixon.
